newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala plans state-asset sales - central banker.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala plans state-asset sales - central banker.

text.p: Guatemala plans to raise $149 million by selling shares in government-owned companies on the local and international stock markets, the country's central bank president said Thursday.

Proceeds from the sales of shares in state-owned electric, telephone and other companies will finance 15 percent of the proposed 1997 government budget, which the finance ministry presented to Congress earlier this week.
"There are many foreign telecommunications businesses interested in investing in Guatemala," Zapata said.
The bank president said the sale no more than 20 percent of the government's ownership of Guatel, the state-owned phone company would support the process of privatization of the industry.

"What we're planning is (selling) some shares in companies," Willy Zapata, president of the central bank, said at a news conference. "We are talking around 900 million quetzales ($149 million) in a budget of 13 billion quetzales ($2.1 billion)."

Zapata said Guatemala would seek the services of a foreign bank to place shares on the market. The government has not yet analyzed the portion of stock to be sold nationally and internationally, he said.

Congress must pass a number of bills before any sales can take place, Zapata said, including legislation creating a superintendency for telecommunications and allowing Guatel to be taken public. Lawmakers are expected to begin considering the telecom legislation next week.
Congress is currently debating a law that would allow private companies to produce and distribute electricity.
